name: Widevine device ID (MediaDrm)
plain: A DRM device ID that some apps read as a stable fingerprint.
meaning: Used for DRM licensing; some builds return a device-unique value that can survive factory reset. Recent Android restricts it per app.

android.persistence: May survive reset on older builds

ios.api_surface: FairPlay has no app-readable device ID

limits.headline: Can tell your Android phone apart using a hidden video protection ID, but not on iPhone
limits.user_action: Nothing. An app can ask for it silently when it starts
can: Get a 32 byte ID tied to your phone's video protection system on Android
Use it as a stable fingerprint across restarts
Link accounts that share the same phone
cannot: Give the same value to every app on recent Android builds; it can differ per app
Exist on iPhone; FairPlay shows apps no device ID
Change when you clear app data; it follows the phone, not the app
limits.differs: Android only. iPhone has no equivalent that apps can see.

story.what_it_is: A hardware ID used by video DRM that apps can sometimes read as a phone fingerprint.

marketing.name: Widevine DRM
marketing.pitch: Pitch: content protection that lets streaming services play licensed video safely on Android and the web.

story.for_you: You never see it. It works behind the scenes so a protected movie will play, and it may also act as a long lasting tag on your phone that survives clearing app data.
story.for_makers: Streaming services need it to give out licences and set quality levels. Because it can stay the same after a reset, some apps use it as a hard to remove device ID for fraud checks and device tracking.

use_cases.example: A streaming app checks your phone's Widevine level before allowing HD or 4K playback.
A service limits how many phones one account can download offline shows to, counting them by device ID.
A fraud team blocks an account sharing scam that signs in from the same hardware over and over.
A cloud gaming app checks that a phone has secure video decoding before it allows protected streams.
A tracker reads a value that outlives a reset to rebuild a profile after you clear your ad ID.
A live sports app uses DRM licences so a match feed cannot be recorded by ripping the stream.

risks: Hard to reset on your own
story.android_note: Newer Android versions restrict this per app, and some phones now return an app specific value.
story.ios_note: iPhone uses Apple's own FairPlay system, so this ID does not exist there.

technical_bounds: Behavior varies by OEM and version
